overview: The Dominican Republic covers the eastern two-thirds of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with Haiti. Its capital, Santo Domingo, founded in the 1490s, is the oldest European city still standing in the Americas. The country became independent in 1844. Baseball is hugely popular, and many top players in the United States come from the Dominican Republic.

geography.text: The Dominican Republic has both the highest point in the Caribbean, Pico Duarte, and the lowest, Lake Enriquillo, a salty lake below sea level. Between its mountain ranges are fertile valleys, and its coasts have beaches on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical, with a hurricane season and cooler air in the mountains of the Cordillera Central.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Humpback whales come to Samaná Bay to breed every winter.

history.text: Columbus reached Hispaniola in 1492, and Santo Domingo became the first Spanish capital in the Americas. The eastern part of the island was ruled by Haiti from 1822 until 1844, when the Dominican Republic declared independence. In the 1900s it was occupied by the United States and then ruled by the dictator Rafael Trujillo for over 30 years.

events.title: Santo Domingo founded
events.text: The first lasting European city in the Americas is founded.

events.title: Independence
events.text: The Dominican Republic breaks away from Haiti.

events.title: US occupation
events.text: US forces occupy the country until 1924.

events.title: Trujillo takes power
events.text: Rafael Trujillo begins three decades of dictatorship.

government.text: The Dominican Republic is a presidential republic. The President is elected every four years. Congress has a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies. It shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti.

economy.text: The Dominican Republic has one of the fastest-growing economies in Latin America. Tourism is huge, especially resorts at Punta Cana. It also exports gold, cigars, cocoa, sugar and medical devices, and many Dominicans abroad send money home.

culture.text: Merengue and bachata, both born in the Dominican Republic, are listed by UNESCO. Santo Domingo was the first European city in the Americas, and its colonial zone has the oldest cathedral in the Americas.

items.title: Merengue
items.text: A fast, two-step dance music, listed by UNESCO in 2016.

items.title: Bachata
items.text: Guitar-based romantic music, listed by UNESCO in 2019.

items.title: Colonial Zone
items.text: Santo Domingo's old town, founded in 1496.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: La bandera, 'the flag': rice, beans and meat, eaten at lunch.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Merengue and bachata, both listed by UNESCO.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: Carnival in February features masked figures called diablos cojuelos.

sport.text: Baseball is the national passion. More players in Major League Baseball come from the Dominican Republic than from any country other than the United States, including stars such as David Ortiz and Pedro Martínez. The country won the World Baseball Classic in 2013.

items.text: Unbeaten winners of the World Baseball Classic.

items.title: David Ortiz
items.text: Won three World Series with the Boston Red Sox.

didYouKnow: Santo Domingo has the oldest cathedral in the Americas, finished in 1541.
Larimar, a blue stone, is found only in the Dominican Republic.
